# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization

**[Date]**

UPMC Health Plan
Appeals Department
**[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]**

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination**
- **Member:** Riley Jennings
- **Member ID:** W995720068
- **Reference number:** POC-39DE00339B-16726
- **Date of denial notice:** August 19, 2026
- **Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
- **Governing policy:** UPMC Provider Manual Chapter G – Utilization Management (https://www.upmchealthplan.com/docs/providers/2025_ProviderManual_G.pdf)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), denied by UPMC Health Plan on August 19, 2026 under reference number POC-39DE00339B-16726. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure my surgeon has documented that I need.

The reason given in the notice was that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I would like to set out what was in fact submitted, and to ask the plan to identify the specific documentation it found missing.

## The policy language I was given does not appear to apply to my surgery

The only policy text I have been able to obtain that the plan connects to this denial reads, in full:

> "• The initial visit between 28 and 32 weeks, and • Following the postpartum visit (1-84 days after delivery) It is important that the dates of all the prenatal visits are included and risk factors are documented."

This language concerns prenatal and postpartum visit documentation. It does not describe any documentation requirement for knee arthroscopy or meniscus surgery, and I cannot map my records to it because it does not apply to my care. This excerpt also appears to be one piece of a longer list of conditions that was not reproduced for me.

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about this: **the plan's actual criteria for CPT 29881 have not been quoted to me.** I am not able to point to a plan sentence and show that I meet it, because I have not been given the sentence. Everything below is therefore argued from my own medical records, not from any threshold I am attributing to the plan. I have not assumed any required duration of conservative care, number of therapy visits, imaging grade, or similar threshold, because the plan has not stated one to me.

## What the submitted records document

My prior authorization packet contains the following, all documented in my chart by my treating providers:

| What the records show | Detail as documented |
|---|---|
| Symptom duration | 9 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest |
| Supervised physical therapy | Quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 10 weeks, May 8, 2026 to July 17, 2026, 16 visits completed — recorded in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Medication trial | NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief |
| Injection | Corticosteroid injection on June 13, 2026, giving 2 weeks of partial relief |
| Imaging | MRI of the knee, July 18, 2026: displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 |
| Function | Locking and giving way; cannot squat or kneel; limited to level walking |
| Physical exam | Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain |
| Surgical risk factors | No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker |
| Treating surgeon | Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery |

This is a documented mechanical problem — a displaced bucket-handle meniscus tear with locking, confirmed on MRI — in a knee whose cartilage is preserved. I completed a full course of supervised physical therapy, a months-long medication trial, and an injection before surgery was requested, and my symptoms continued. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

If any of these items did not reach the reviewer, I am asking that the plan tell me which one, so my providers and I can supply it. A determination that documentation is incomplete should be accompanied by an identification of what is missing, and I have not received that.

## Request for the criteria actually applied

**I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule, guideline, or criterion the plan relied on to deny this request.** If the review was performed using licensed clinical review criteria such as InterQual, I am specifically asking for **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, together with the complete list of documentation elements required for CPT 29881 and an identification of which of those elements were found absent from my file. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules entitle me to the specific rule or criterion relied on in denying my claim. Until I receive it, I cannot fully respond to the basis for this decision, and I ask that my appeal rights be preserved accordingly.

## What I am asking for

I ask UPMC Health Plan to:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29881 as requested by Lindqvist, MD; or
2. If the plan maintains the denial, provide me in writing with the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied, and a specific list of the documents or findings the plan considers missing, so they can be submitted; and
3. Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, by **February 15, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice, and I will follow the filing instructions set out in that notice.

Please contact me if anything further is needed. My surgeon's office has confirmed it will provide any additional records the plan identifies.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Riley Jennings**
